newsitem.title: SPAIN: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN PIPS ARCH-RIVAL CRIVILLE FOR POLE.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN PIPS ARCH-RIVAL CRIVILLE FOR POLE.

text.p: Michael Doohan moved a step closer to his third consecutive world championship after knocking arch-rival Alex Criville off pole position in the final minutes of practice for the Grand Prix of Catalonia on Saturday.
It was a major psychological victory for Doohan, who needs only to finish second in Sunday's race to guarantee the title.
Doohan, a disappointing eighth in practice on Friday, had earlier seen Spaniard Criville improve on the previous fastest time set by Luca Cadalora of Italy.
But with the qualifying session coming to an end, the Australian went a further 10th of a second faster to secure his seventh pole position of the season.
"It would be nice to win, but I'll be concentrating on sticking close to Alex," said Doohan, who will also take the title if Criville gets less than seven points more than him from the race.
Cadalora was pushed down to third, and fell while attempting a difficult overtaking manouevre around Criville.
The Italian got up swiftly from his fall and said he would be on the starting grid.
"It was my last opportunity to take pole position," said Cadalora. "It was my first fall of the championship, but I'm in condition to win."
Local rider Carlos Checa completes the front line of the starting grid, while Frenchman Jean-Michel Bayle and Brazilian Alexandre Barros are in fifth and sixth respectively.
